streams.status_detail: PR #82 merged into main as a19252bb4df28e2733b6b5180c8938792c040e63. Its exact-head quality CI 45875671834 and actual CPU-thread workflow 45875671867 both succeeded. The verifier checks a strict canonical checkpoint payload, detached Ed25519 signature against caller-supplied trusted keys, expected store identity, and local event-chain hash/count; it rejects lower generations and same-sequence equivocation and marks bootstrap-only verification explicitly when no trusted high-water state is supplied. The caller must atomically persist returned state outside the SQLite rollback domain. Post-merge main quality CI 45875861427 and Pages build/deploy 45875861440 succeeded. No production signer, external high-water authority, authorized sensor/lab dataset, site-approved Water Safety Plan limits or field validation exists. A public-source Georgia monitoring inventory found existing NEA surface-water (238 locations) and groundwater (72 points) monitoring disclosures, a separate monthly Black Sea network (14 points in the July 2026 update), and a utility laboratory network described as 8 regional plus 35 service-centre labs. These are source-reported network/process facts, not sample-level data or proof of drinking-water safety. No machine-readable sample dataset or data dictionary was identified in the pages inspected; no raw result was imported. Discovery update 2026-11-27: the 2025 UNECE/WHO Georgia report states groundwater results have been available electronically since 2022, records 394 laboratory samples from 72 groundwater points in 2024, and reports 2024 surface-water sampling at 331 points on 137 water bodies. It separately reports 40.3% E. coli non-compliance in drinking-water samples for 2024, mainly microbiological, with rural small systems included; the table does not expose the denominator. NEA announced a 2021-2025 groundwater report and nitrate-risk field methodology on 2026-11-26 and linked a RAR archive that has not yet been inspected. WIS C10/C11 provide historical 2004-2018 aggregate indicators; Hydromet lists a water-quality-points map/table whose fields remain unverified. These discoveries narrow the earlier data-access blocker but do not establish a current sample-level API or reuse permission. No raw observations were imported. The UNECE/WHO submission also states that automatic groundwater stations were installed in 11 district units across 8 regional administrations during 2022-2024, 12 groundwater bulletins were published, and groundwater used as a drinking-water source was generally assessed as good quality with isolated microbiological exceedances. This countervailing source-reported evidence is recorded to avoid overstatement. The UNECE/WHO drinking-water section contains two distinct E. coli reference frames: narrative values for 2021-2022/2023/2024 and table values labelled 2005/2019/2024. They are not combined into one trend because the sample denominator and urban/rural breakdown are absent. A 2026-08-31 Government Resolution No.424 now provides a primary legal basis for a prospective well-registration source effective 2026-09-01, limited to fresh drinking-water extraction wells deeper than 20 m; pre-existing wells are outside the legal scope and NEA says household wells are excluded. The passport includes owner identity/contact data and optional field/lab result attachments, so only privacy-reviewed de-identified access can be considered. The register itself and public reuse terms remain unverified. 2026-11-27 update: MEPA's GIS catalogue exposes NEA122, a point-geometry groundwater monitoring layer classified public/free (catalogue date 2026-03-06), but its row lists SQL SDE/local storage and no portal URL; the payload and reuse licence remain unverified. NEA's 2026-06-09 notice describes automatic monitored-well stations and field data-registration/documentation procedures in Tianeti. Article 32 assigns environmental-water monitoring data to NEA and drinking-water quality state control to the National Food Safety Agency. No coordinates or sample rows were imported. Run 26 (2026-11-27): primary-source audit compared NEA's 2025-09-18 network disclosure (72 groundwater points, 238 surface-water locations, 12 Black Sea locations) with the 2025 annual report (124 groundwater monitoring points: 74 planned + 50 field-instrumental; 681 lab samples from 74 points; nitrate field studies at 50 points = 19 wells + 30 springs + 1 control well; 73 points with listed parameter coverage; separate surface water 238 points / 2,571 samples). These counts are different reporting frames; 72→74 is not treated as a trend or unique-point increase. The Georgian term “საკონტროლო ჭა” was corrected from “household well” to “control well”: documentation correction merged in PR #149 as 2469d0c; the full aggregate data/schema/test correction remains Draft PR #144 at head 95c69d94d2a97197d2a5199abe22eec0c9248abf. Exact-head Quality CI 45993708487 and CPU-thread workflow 45993708489 succeeded. The 2021–2025 RAR remains unextracted; no sample-level data or reuse terms were obtained. Run 31 (2026-11-27): the official NEA Geology bulletin index was rechecked and a distinct November 2021 information hydrogeological bulletin listing plus direct file endpoint were recorded in PR #164. The web reader rejected the 22,990,164-byte response as too large and container-side DNS retrieval failed; no file payload bytes, contents, hash, sample schema or reuse terms were inspected. This historical bulletin is distinct from the 2021–2025 RAR. The restore-drill CLI validates a same-host temporary filesystem round-trip only; it does not validate encrypted off-host storage, provider object versions, key recovery or clean-host disaster recovery.
A matching unsigned manifest and matching artifact hashes do not authenticate provenance; an attacker able to replace both files and the manifest can recompute the hashes.
A valid detached signature does not prove that a signed backup is the newest; rollback/freeze protection requires separately trusted monotonic state and freshness policy.
The local verifier authenticates exact manifest bytes only when the caller's public key is independently trusted; key compromise, revocation and rotation are not managed here.
A schema-valid or self-declared restore attestation is not proof: the caller must independently verify every evidence signature and trust anchor.
Restoring a backup generation older than the trusted high-water mark can roll back accepted state; the gate blocks this case and any decrease of high-water state.
